## Purpose
Track the incremental modernization of Tempo based on the independent architecture audit of main at `d4dbf28da5b6e95db8da1acfd9fecd4655821296` (2026-10-11). **Architecture decision: modular monolith with isolated background/model workers, not a rewrite or independently deployed domain microservices.**

This is a coordination/roadmap issue, **not authorization to implement every stage in one PR**. Preserve the existing authoritative PostgreSQL transaction model, command and logical review receipts, queue issuance, generation fences, browser intent recovery, and native durability proofs.

## Goals and architectural invariants
- Studying and saving an already prepared review must not depend on unrelated imports, analytics, evidence rebuilds, or bulk browser indexing.
- A review's schedule/history/queue/evidence/receipt effects remain atomic. PostgreSQL is authoritative; the browser retains original intent and owns only volatile view/attempt installation.
- Only an issued head or exact server-authorized continuation may advance a session; stale callbacks cannot replace the current attempt.
- Dependency direction: **HTTP/Celery adapters → application services → pure domain logic + explicit PostgreSQL repositories**. Domain/application services must not import `main.py` or Celery entry points.
- Pure scheduling, readiness, policy reach, valuation and position-identity logic should be independently testable without Redis, Docker or a database.
- Keep one PostgreSQL database and existing operational worker isolation initially. Separate containers/processes only for measured runtime isolation needs.
- No reliability mechanism may be removed without a replacement proof covering its invariant, interruption/restart, concurrency, and old pending state.

## Stages and tracking

### 0 — Stabilize before structural changes
- [ ] Reconcile and qualify existing issue #144 / PR #146 (first-enqueue authoritative identity).
- [ ] Reconcile and qualify PR #191 (joined outbox result/continuation preservation).
- [ ] Resolve issue #190 (bulk browser computation blocks foreground work); verify native worker capacity, cancellation and parity on a representative workload.
- [ ] Diagnose the failed prefix-diagnostics browser case in main CI run 38138170016; establish clean baseline without assuming flakiness.
- [ ] Reconcile existing structural-recovery work (#187–#189) separately; do not absorb it into modularization.
- [ ] Assign a single integration owner for migration collisions (main already has 046; #117/#184 and other branches propose competing numbers).

### 1 — Contract-first pure domain boundaries
- [ ] Inventory existing public/persisted contracts and unresolved browser intents; define compatibility fixtures and explicit clocks/source versions.
- [ ] Extract only genuinely pure scheduling, readiness, reach, valuation, position/policy identity logic into independently testable in-process modules/packages where justified.
- [ ] Add dependency-direction checks with documented transitional exceptions.
- [ ] Correct stale SQLite-first architecture guidance in `backend/app/README.md`; document Python runtime pin mismatch (project >=3.14 vs CI 3.12.14).

### 2 — Backend training application (first major structural extraction)
- [ ] Move `main._apply_review` and related application orchestration behind a typed internal training application interface; keep routes thin.
- [ ] Remove command/queue service back-imports of `main` via compatibility-preserving wrappers.
- [ ] Make repository mutation ownership and transaction/lock order explicit.
- [ ] Prove unchanged HTTP/persisted contracts, atomic review settlement, conflict/replay, optional authorized continuation, native PostgreSQL concurrency and lost-response recovery.

### 3 — Frontend session and intent ownership
- [ ] Define one coordinator for committed/conflicted/pending settlement and attempt/view-owned advancement; preserve separate board shell ownership.
- [ ] Characterize the suspected cross-tab whole-array outbox lost-update race with native two-tab tests before classifying it as confirmed.
- [ ] If proven, introduce keyed transactional browser intent storage with restartable, nondestructive migration of unresolved envelopes.
- [ ] Preserve offline replay, opening evidence provenance, late-response fencing, keyboard/drag and structural publication semantics.

### 4 — Background isolation and bounded publication
- [ ] Move product-specific failure projections out of generic durable-task infrastructure through explicit registered domain adapters.
- [ ] Make capture → compute (outside DB transaction) → fenced commit boundaries explicit for existing slices.
- [ ] Inventory aggregate DB pool/CPU budgets; profile queue and game-derivation hotspots before optimization.
- [ ] Prove crash/restart, generation replacement, foreground priority, idempotent replay and publication visibility.

### 5 — Test cost and qualification
- [ ] Investigate costly CLI subprocess grouping and repeated runtime inventory; move/optimize only with case-ID coverage equivalence.
- [ ] Preserve source-selected CI planning, full native PostgreSQL/browser durability proofs and exact-candidate provenance.
- [ ] Report comparable wall-clock before/after setup, execution, wait and cleanup, without weakening timeouts or assertions.

### 6 — Future product features (separate scope)
- [ ] After stable contracts, integrate position inventory (#117), source/provider adapters (#181), settings/weights (#184) and global introduction budgeting through coherent versioned snapshots and explicit fenced queue admission.
- [ ] Treat shadow valuation/readiness as estimates, not authorization; retain unknown probability mass and policy-specific identity.
- [ ] Serialize migration allocation and shared-schema integration.

### 7 — Conditional retirement only
- [ ] Consider direct API foreground writes / removing Redis from ordinary review delivery **only** after a separate security, role, admission, outage and concurrency proof.
- [ ] Retire legacy adapters/journals only when historical compatibility and all protected invariants are demonstrated.

## Execution rules
1. Create **separate bounded implementation issues/PRs** for stages and distinct invariant-bearing subprojects. Link them here; do not open a giant implementation PR.
2. Stage 0 is the gate for major structural work; read-only characterization and Stage 1 pure-contract work may run in parallel.
3. One owner at a time for shared schema/migrations, command gateway, admission, CI planner, and cross-cutting training state. Independent domain work may proceed against frozen contracts.
4. Use isolated checkouts, never alter live study resources, and qualify each exact head/base/integration candidate per `CONTRIBUTING.md` and `docs/testing.md`.
5. Every extraction must preserve user behavior, historical data, unresolved browser intents, and named regressions. Record rollback path before merging.
6. No speculative event bus, service-per-domain, separate domain database, or wholesale rewrite.

## Completion criteria
- [ ] Each stage has linked, independently reviewed and qualified implementation issues/PRs or an explicit decision to defer.
- [ ] Training critical-path dependencies and state ownership are documented and enforced; background failures do not block authorized prepared study.
- [ ] Pure domain packages run independent tests without infrastructure; dependency rules prevent application → HTTP/worker back-imports.
- [ ] Transaction, issuance, replay, offline, multi-tab, worker crash and stale-publication guarantees remain covered by native tests.
- [ ] CI proof inventory remains intact, and representative iteration cost and foreground responsiveness are measured.
- [ ] Architecture documentation matches the implemented system; remaining retirement candidates are explicitly justified/deferred.

## Audit provenance
Independent read-only audit: remote main `d4dbf28da5b6e95db8da1acfd9fecd4655821296` (2026-10-11), with source/dependency measurements, ownership matrix, failure traces, CI evidence and stage roadmap supplied in the architecture report. Current deployed study runtime and unmerged PRs were **not** assumed equivalent to that revision. Refresh main and open PR status before each stage; the audit is a baseline, not a perpetual live inventory.

## CI isolation audit follow-ups (12 October 2026)

Documentation: [audit](https://github.com/aaweaver-actuary/tempo/blob/main/docs/architecture/ci-isolation/audit-report.md) · [issue specifications](https://github.com/aaweaver-actuary/tempo/blob/main/docs/architecture/ci-isolation/issue-specs.md) · [parallel assignments](https://github.com/aaweaver-actuary/tempo/blob/main/docs/architecture/ci-isolation/parallel-impl.md).

Created bounded issues: #198 (B00 current-main browser failures), #199 (B01 controlled browser host), #200 (B02 pure domain boundaries), #201 (B03 harness ownership), #202 (B04 shadow CI selection), #203 (B05 fresh complete merge gate), #204 (B06 scheduling-review port), #205 (B07 native proof IDs). Start #198/#199/#200 independently. Existing PG/browser CI jobs are already separate; the work is fixture/dependency decoupling, not duplicate job splitting. Keep current quality protection until #202 shadow evidence and separately approved #203 enforcement.

Implementation reconciliation snapshot (2026-10-12): merged #172 (prepared review continuation), #195 (durable Study-only mode; live acceptance pending), #197 (default-off additional opening frontier, not activated), and #213 (agent checkout cleanup policy). CI isolation: B00/#198 → open #207 ready for review and #211 draft/blocked; B01/#199 → draft #212; B02/#200 → draft #206. B03–B07 (#201–#205) have open implementation issues; no corresponding implementation PR verified in this pass. Stage-0 #146/#144 and #191 are open, not merged. Browser structural #187–#189 remain separate and unmerged. None of these PR links imply production deployment, end-to-end isolation, or closure of a roadmap stage. Maintain separate statuses: designed → PR implemented → qualified → merged → operationally verified.

Additional reconciliation (2026-10-12): CI antecedents merged #95 (narrow browser smoke), #96 (separate lifecycle), #147 (4-shard browser parallelism). B03–B07 (#201–#205): no dedicated implementation PR identified by repository search; not equivalent to 'no work exists'. Stage-0 #144/#146 and #191 remain open/unmerged. Foreground mitigation foundations merged #83/#120/#122/#172/#195, but #190 representative isolation proof is outstanding. Frontend structural #187/#188/#189 are unmerged stacked recovery work, not stage-3 completion. Pure read-only domain foundations #176 and #178 merged; #177 evaluation harness remains open. Preserve distinction between antecedent, implementation, qualification, merge, and operational proof.

**Code-level architecture finding (main inspected 2026-10-12):** confirmed `review_commands.py:54 → main._apply_review` (`main.py:3021-3305`), and `services/postgres_queue_refresh.py:804 → main` with multiple helper calls (360-423,605-659,891-994). The former is a worker→HTTP composition-root reverse dependency; the latter keeps essential queue refresh coupled to main even in Study-only mode. Transaction path: `main.py:2955-2997` → `command_dispatch.py:19-77` → `tasks.py:178-218` → `command_gateway.py:229-365` → `review_commands.py:52-109` → `_apply_review`. `review_commands.py:103-108` writes prepared continuation into attempt receipt within the same transaction. `command_gateway.py:235-246` performs queue wake only after inner commit. #204 should own review application extraction; separately inventory/extract queue-refresh helper ownership (avoid silently broadening #204). Source inspection only; no test or deployed-runtime proof.

**Execution strategy update (2026-10-12):** Three independent read-only architecture audits now tracked as #217 (A: backend review/queue transaction), #218 (B: worker/resource contention), and #219 (C: frontend session/intent ownership). Run in parallel, with A owning proposed shared review/queue interfaces and B/C avoiding changes to them. After evidence and contract freeze, implementation follows in separate PRs: existing #204 (review application) and new #220 (essential queue application), then native failure-injection qualification. Keep Stage 0 gates #144/#146, #191, #190 and B00 explicit. No structural implementation authorized merely by opening audit issues. Status stages: characterized → implemented → exact candidate qualified → merged → operationally verified.

title: Architecture modernization roadmap: modular monolith, state ownership, and reliable study isolation
